title: feat(browser): add autonomous collaboration fabric
body:
## Summary
- stack on exact Browser coordination baseline `739ba8196f0e37f8c0dca1f863ee60aa606bbedc`
- add a zero-authority collaboration fabric for continuous multi-agent work
- model typed causal messages, task/progress ledgers, immutable artifact refs, compact handoff capsules and advisory anti-duplication claims
- wire the collaboration fabric directly into `BrowserBrainContinuousCoordinator`
- expose Brain APIs for collaboration tasks, progress, messages, artifacts, claims, handoffs and autonomous continuation decisions
- make ordinary agent work explicitly unbounded: `work_cycle_limit: null`, `external_confirmation_gate: false`, `external_prompt_required_for_continuation: false`, `idle_wait_allowed: false`

## Autonomy invariant
Useful agent work must continue without waiting for a user message or approval. Empty work queues trigger autonomous discovery; ready work is claimed; blockers trigger replanning; claimed work triggers complementary discovery; terminal objectives trigger discovery of the next objective. A completed task is never a terminal service state.

Conversation rollover/restart is continuity plumbing, not a work limit: durable state is used to continue in the successor context automatically.

## Authority boundary
This does **not** create a second scheduler, command lease, hidden effect queue or Browser executor. Collaboration messages, claims, artifacts and memory carry zero execution authority. Physical effects still flow through the existing machine lease/exact-target/runtime-fence path, and ambiguous destructive effects are not blindly retried.

## Tests
- typed message idempotency and collision rejection
- anti-duplication claims stay advisory and permit independent verification
- immutable artifact provenance
- compact handoff without transcript copying
- empty/ready/blocked/terminal contexts always choose an autonomous next action
- progress ledger remains zero-authority
- continuous coordinator exposes the unbounded autonomous collaboration contract

## Next memory slice
Persist collaboration checkpoints/episodic trajectories and add hybrid retrieval/promotion without introducing a new scheduler or any user-confirmation dependency.

title: perf(browser): fence shared semantic cache on runtime lifecycle
body:
## Summary
- stack on exact-green #351 head `8ce05dfe2c632d60b721c0751c437d3fc570d4a9`
- add one idempotent lifecycle binder for the shared generation-fenced native semantic runtime cache
- invalidate cached backend-node hints immediately on main-frame navigation, renderer loss, or WebContents destruction
- leave subframe navigation alone so unrelated frame churn does not evict a valid main-frame cache
- remove lifecycle listeners on destruction and permit a future successor WebContents object to bind independently

## Why
#351 made capture and later semantic resolution share one process-local cache, but explicit invalidation was still manual. This slice establishes the fail-closed lifecycle boundary needed before wiring the cache into native semantic command call sites: stale semantic hints are removed as soon as the Browser runtime reports a navigation/incarnation-loss edge, rather than waiting for a later lookup to discover generation drift.

## Safety
- source-only draft
- no production DDL / Edge deploy / release / cutover
- no Browser reset/close or live actuation
- invalidation only removes observation hints; it cannot grant authority
- no scheduler, lease, effect execution, hidden queue or automatic retry authority
- DB lease and final runtime/effect fence remain unchanged

## Tests
- binding is idempotent
- main-frame navigation evicts cache so the next lookup performs fresh full-tree resolution
- subframe navigation preserves the main-frame cache and narrow partial revalidation
- renderer loss and destruction evict cache
- destruction removes listeners
- lifecycle snapshot proves zero authority / zero automatic retry
